summary: A white memorial light at Empire, Michigan, built by family and friends after Robert H. Manning's death in 1989; a private aid, open grounds, closed tower.

light.note: First illumination disputed: 1990 (Northern Michigan History, which says dedicated 1991) or 1991 (Lighthouse Friends, which gives the dedication year; Rowlett and US-Lighthouses give 1991 for the light).

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed; no tours. Private aid to navigation maintained seasonally, mid-April to mid-November.

facts.agency: Private aid to navigation; Village of Empire (Rowlett) or Town of Empire (Lighthouse Friends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Northern Michigan History says the light was illuminated in 1990 and dedicated in 1991. Lighthouse Friends gives 1991 as the dedication year; Rowlett and US-Lighthouses give 1991 for the light. Not resolved; the story gives the year as disputed and cites each source. The station record's 1990 (Wikidata/ENC) matches NMH only.
Rowlett names the Village of Empire as owner and site manager; Lighthouse Friends names the Town of Empire. The record's agency is empty.
The record gives 11.0 m; Rowlett gives about 35 ft (11 m); US-Lighthouses gives 35 ft. Consistent with the record.

notes_for_editor:
1. Thin station: the sources repeat the same few facts. The story is short and has no headings.
2. Dates: 1990 (Northern Michigan History; the record's Wikidata/ENC value) vs 1991 (Lighthouse Friends, Rowlett, US-Lighthouses). Wikipedia says lit 1990 and cites a Terry Pepper page that returned HTTP 404 when checked; Wikipedia was not cited.
3. Owner: Village of Empire (Rowlett) vs Town of Empire (Lighthouse Friends). Not resolved.
4. The Northern Michigan History article is a local feature, not a primary record; cited as such.
5. The Lake Havasu City, Arizona replica (related record us-az-robert-h-manning) appears only in Wikipedia; not checked and not in the story.
6. Lighthouse Friends is all-rights-reserved; facts only, with prose written here. Its one line on the seasonal light is paraphrased.
7. No Coast Guard Light List entry was read directly; the seasonal dates come from Lighthouse Friends and Northern Michigan History.
8. Robert Manning is a private person who died in 1989; the story names him only as the memorial's subject, with the details the published sources print.

10. Fact-check pass (2026-10-28): the story no longer says the sources disagree on the 'first showed' date only; Lighthouse Friends' 1991 is a dedication date, so the story gives it as one.
